messages:
Anna (CS): Quick sync — prepping Acme Enterprise account QBR. Main asks: 1) 90-day spend forecast, 2) onboarding completion % and blockers, 3) any alerts or sudden token burn spikes. @Tara (FinOps) can you surface alerts?
Miguel (SE): On it. I can export per-route token counts and embeddings spend by customer tag. Will share a table by EOD. Any specific forecast window? 30/60/90 days?
Tara (FinOps): 90-day preferred. Also check credits threshold alerts from the last 14 days — they had a surge last week. I'll pull rolling burn and projected runway.
Jess (Onboarding): Onboarding status: 7/10 milestones complete, docs integration stalled on SSO testing. Customer asked for dedicated onboarding session next Wed. Might affect activation-based discounts if delayed.
Anna (CS): Noted. Activation discount timeline could impact renewal negotiation. If onboarding slips, flag renewal risk.
Miguel (SE): Quick export command I used:
```
rbill export --acct acme-enterprise --metrics tokens,embeddings --since 2026-09-01 --group-by route --format csv
```
I attached a short CSV to the internal doc (link in thread).
Tara (FinOps): Raw numbers: last 7 days avg token/day = 1.8M, embeddings ops/day = 120k. Burn rate jumped 42% after their feature flag went live. Projected 90-day spend if unchanged = $74k (vs. current committed $55k).
OpsBot: alert: acme-enterprise hit 85% of committed credits threshold (reason: high-embeddings request burst). Alert details: https://alerts.redwood/acme/4573
Miguel (SE): The embeddings are coming from a batch job hitting multiple long sequences. We can recommend quantized model or caching. Quick suggestion: lower embedding window from 4096 -> 2048 for non-critical paths, should cut tokens ~30%.
Tara (FinOps): If they accept caching + window reduction, forecast drops to ~$54k — back within commit. But need sign-off from product/engineers and validation that accuracy ok.
Jess (Onboarding): I'll schedule the extra onboarding session and include an ops walkthrough to explain batching/caching options. Also will ask for permission to run a controlled experiment next week.
Anna (CS): Action items: Miguel to draft recommended config changes + expected savings (due tomorrow), Tara to produce a 90-day scenario table (baseline, with-optimizations, worst-case), Jess to schedule onboarding + experiment, I'll own renewal-facing note about potential risk and mitigation.
Miguel (SE): Drafted config diff snippet for their infra team:
```
# reduce embedding window for background index updates
EMBED_WINDOW=2048
BATCH_CONCURRENCY=8  # tune down from 16 during peak
CACHE_PREFIX_TTL=86400  # keep prefix cache for 24h
```
Tara (FinOps): I'll include a slide in the QBR deck showing projected savings and alert history. Also recommend a 2-week credit buffer in their contract to avoid urgent outages.
Anna (CS): Perfect. If we can get the experiment results next Friday we can finalize the renewal playbook and present at QBR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
__notes: Generated Slack thread for customer-success channel about QBR prep, token economics, onboarding status, and budget alerts. Single-string messages field as required. No title field included.
